newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 72,000t of U.S. wheat - trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 72,000t of U.S. wheat - trade.

text.p: The Taiwan Flour Mills Association is expected to tender for 72,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat next week while corn and soybean buyers are likely to stay on the sidelines, traders said on Friday.
Flour Mills association official Lu Wei-chih told Reuters they will probably buy the wheat in two shipments.
The first shipment of 34,000 tonnes would be delivered from December 15 from the U.S. Gulf, he said. The second shipment of 38,000 tonnes would be for delivery from December 30 from the U.S. Gulf.
No exact date for the tender has been set, but Lu said the association would try to place the tender by December 6.
Traders said expectations by buyers that corn and soybean futures prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) could fall further was behind their adoption of a wait-and-see stance in the market.
"Taiwan's corn and soybean buyers are likely to stay sidelined until clear market indications become available," a trader said.
Taiwan's soymeal price on Friday for Taipei delivery was quoted unchanged at T$9.70-$9.90 a kg, dealers said.
The corn powders price was at T$7.05 a kg for Taipei delivery, down from between T$7.30 to $7.40 last week.
The local flour price on Friday was quoted unchanged between T$14.55 to $15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, dealers said.
The Pacific Northwest to Taiwan freight cost was quoted at about US$11.00 a tonne while Gulf of Mexico was about $20.00 to $21.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
